primary_bug.summary: Making createChildren (the implementation behind the public Node.getChildren() API) scan JSX source files with the JSX language variant changes the token stream getChildren() emits for JSX files — most visibly, `</` is now a single LessThanSlashToken instead of the previous LessThanToken + SlashToken pair, and JSX-variant scanning re-tiles trivia/token ranges differently in addSyntheticNodes' `while (pos < end) { scanner.scan(); pos = getTokenEnd() }` loop. getChildren() is a widely-consumed public API; downstream tools that recursively walk it over JSX ASTs (typescript-eslint, eslint-stylistic) crash with 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded' on the changed/mis-tiled child stream. The bug does NOT surface in TypeScript's own test suite (only two fourslash baselines needed updating) — it manifests almost entirely downstream, which is why it shipped in 5.9.x and was fully reverted (#62423, fixing regression #62188).
primary_bug.locus: createChildren ~L507-529: `const languageVariant = sourceFile?.languageVariant ?? LanguageVariant.Standard; scanner.setText(...); scanner.setLanguageVariant(languageVariant);` feeding addSyntheticNodes' scan loop (L535-553). The completions.ts/utilities.ts SlashToken->LessThanSlashToken edits are the downstream ripple of the same tokenization change.
primary_bug.must_flag: A reviewer catches the primary bug if it identifies that switching createChildren/getChildren to the JSX language variant CHANGES the observable token children that the public getChildren() API returns for JSX files, and that this risks breaking or crashing DOWNSTREAM / external AST consumers (e.g. typescript-eslint, eslint, other tools that walk getChildren) that depend on the prior tokenization — OR names a concrete failure mode of the new scanning that produces the crash (malformed/overlapping/mis-tiled synthetic children, or an addSyntheticNodes scan that fails to advance `pos` and loops, yielding a child stream that sends recursive walkers into unbounded recursion). Equivalent framings that count: 'getChildren is public API and this silently changes its output for JSX, a breaking change for consumers'; 'downstream tools relying on <,/ as separate tokens will break when they get LessThanSlashToken'; 'the tests pass but external consumers of getChildren over JSX will crash/recurse'. Merely describing WHAT the change does (uses JSX variant, updates token kinds), praising its internal consistency, or noting the token-kind edits match — WITHOUT identifying the downstream/public-API breakage or a concrete crash mechanism — does NOT count.
primary_bug.source: revert PR #62423 ('Revert PR 61928', Fixes #62188: 'I'm not sure if it's worth the crashing it seems to be causing downstream. Some things have been fixed, but not everything.', linking typescript-eslint#11455 and eslint-stylistic#915) + regression issue #62188 ('RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded for 5.9.x' running `eslint src && tsc --noEmit`, ok on 5.8.x). Verified against the checkout at merge 02672d2: createChildren sets the JSX variant; addSyntheticNodes drives a plain scanner.scan() loop over the range.
primary_bug.difficulty: VERY HARD — a downstream-only regression. The diff is small, internally consistent (every closing-element SlashToken->LessThanSlashToken edit matches the new tokenization), addresses a real correctness gap (getChildren previously mis-tokenized `</`), passes TypeScript's own suite with only baseline churn, and even had a human reviewer approve after a minor optional-typing nit. Catching it requires either (a) domain knowledge that getChildren() is a load-bearing public API consumed by external tooling and that changing its JSX tokenization is a breaking behavioral change, or (b) retrieving the revert/issue from git history. Expect very low true recall; a genuine, diff-grounded catch is a strong signal. Tools that merely retrieve-and-parrot '#62423 reverted this' without a mechanism should be graded generously only if they name the downstream-consumer breakage.

known_safe.summary: `languageVariant?: LanguageVariant` is declared OPTIONAL on SourceFileLike (types.ts and the public d.ts baseline). This is correct and deliberate — it is exactly what human reviewer DanielRosenwasser requested ('I would personally just declare languageVariant as optional in SourceFileLike'), and optionality avoids breaking the many existing SourceFileLike implementers. Flagging 'languageVariant should be required' or 'making it optional is a mistake' is a false positive.

`sourceFile?.languageVariant ?? LanguageVariant.Standard` safely handles both a missing sourceFile and a SourceFileLike that does not set languageVariant (defaulting to Standard). Flagging an NPE / 'undefined languageVariant crashes' / 'unhandled undefined' here is a false positive — the optional chain and nullish coalescing guard it.

The SlashToken -> LessThanSlashToken updates for JSX CLOSING-element handling (completions.ts getJsxClosingTagCompletion L1598, the JsxClosingElement cases L3520/L5808, and utilities.ts isInsideJsxElementOrAttribute L1892 / the added case in isInsideJsxElement L1937) are internally CONSISTENT with the new JSX tokenization, where a closing-tag `</` scans as a single LessThanSlashToken. Flagging these closing-element edits as 'breaks closing-tag detection' or 'wrong token kind' is a false positive against the new tokenization. (NOTE: the completions.ts L3511 case that checks `parent.kind === JsxSelfClosingElement` under LessThanSlashToken is a legitimate gray area — a self-closing element's `/` is a plain SlashToken, not `</` — so a finding that specifically argues the SELF-CLOSING case no longer matches is a candidate valid-other, not covered by this known_safe.)

createChildren DOES reset the shared scanner on the normal path: `scanner.setText(undefined); scanner.setLanguageVariant(LanguageVariant.Standard);` at the end. Claiming 'the JSX language variant is never reset and permanently corrupts the shared scanner for all later getChildren calls' is a false positive on the happy path. (The genuine, narrower issue — the reset is not in a try/finally, so a throw from node.forEachChild/addSyntheticNodes leaks the JSX variant — is a candidate valid-other, distinct from the primary.)
